events.title: The Fourth Lateran Council opens
events.shortBlurb: The greatest council of the medieval West opened in Rome under Pope Innocent III…
body: Summoned by the bull Vineam Domini of April 1213, the Fourth Lateran Council opened on 11 November 1215 in the Lateran basilica, Innocent III preaching on the words 'With desire I have desired to eat this pasch with you.' Some 400 bishops, more than 800 abbots and priors, and the envoys of Christian princes made it the greatest assembly of the medieval Church, reckoned the twelfth general council.

Its seventy decrees opened with the confession Firmiter, which employed the word transubstantiation for the change of the bread and wine into Christ's body and blood. The twenty-first canon, Omnis utriusque sexus, bound every believer to confess to his own priest and to receive the Eucharist at least once a year at Easter; others legislated against heresy and ordered Jews and Saracens marked out by their dress.

The council further decreed the reform of the clergy, the provision of preachers for the people, and a new crusade for the deliverance of the Holy Land. Innocent died at Perugia in July 1216, but his council's canons passed into the law and life of the Church and ordered Catholic practice for centuries.
